name: Georgian Jewellery
summary: Jewels of the Hanoverian reigns: foil-backed gems and paste in closed silver and gold settings, bright cut steel, pierced bows and flower sprays. They were made by hand to shine in candlelight.

philosophy.core_thesis: In candlelight a jewel must return the flame. A sheet of foil under the stone and a closed setting make a small gem glow like a large one.
design_principles: Back each stone with a thin sheet of coloured foil inside a closed box setting, so that the stone returns candlelight.
Set the face of a stone in silver and make the back of the piece in gold. Silver keeps a white stone clear, and gold lies on the skin.
Cut diamonds and paste in the old mine cut or the rose cut, with a high crown and many small facets.
Make a rivière as one line of graduated stones, with the largest stone at the centre and a collet round each stone.
Pierce and chase the metal into bows, ribbons and sprays of flowers that follow the curves of the rococo.
Rivet small faceted steel studs to a plate for cut steel, a bright jewel that costs far less than a diamond one.
Hang each piece on a ribbon, a slide or a short chain so that it sits at the throat, the ear or the bodice.
Keep the back of each piece plain or engraved, because a closed setting has no open back.
anti_patterns: Open-backed claw settings that show the point of the stone
Platinum or white gold, which no workshop used yet
Modern brilliant cuts with a flat crown

silhouette.shape: A small, flat, closed jewel: a bow, a flower spray or a three-drop earring, set close to the dress and made for a candlelit room.
silhouette.line: Curved and pierced: ribbons, leaves and swags, with the stones set in a graduated row.
silhouette.fit: Close to the body: a rivière sits at the base of the neck, a bow brooch lies flat on the bodice.
silhouette.proportion: Rivière stones graduate from about 4 mm at the clasp to about 14 mm at the centre. A bow brooch is 5 to 8 cm wide.
rules: Wear a rivière close at the base of the neck, with the largest stone at the front.
Hang a girandole earring in three drops under a bow or a cluster.
Pin a bow brooch at the centre of the bodice or on the stomacher.
Tie a pendant cross or a locket on a ribbon of velvet at the throat.

fabrics.rule: Pair foiled paste and gems with silver on the face and gold behind; use cut steel and pinchbeck for the cheaper, daily jewel.

methods: closed collet settings with a coloured foil behind each stone
silver front over a gold back
hand-pierced and chased bows and sprays
riveted cut-steel studs on a plate
rivière of graduated collets joined by small links
hair and enamel under a crystal for a mourning piece
construction.closures: A hook and eye or a tongue clasp on a necklace; a pin and a C-clasp on a brooch; a wire hook on an earring.
construction.details: Ribbon bows, giardinetto flower sprays, a table-cut garnet or a rose-cut diamond at the centre, and a plain engraved back.

surface.pattern: Flower sprays, bows and ribbons, in rows of equal collets; a mourning piece carries a lock of hair or a monogram.
surface.gloss: High on the stones and the polished silver; the foil gives a deep, even glow of 70 to 90 GU.
surface.wear: Silver tarnishes to grey, foil loses its silver and the stone goes dull; a worn piece shows its age and keeps its value.

palette.strategy: White silver and yellow gold as the ground, with one red, green or blue paste stone and the grey of steel.

processes: hand cutting of stones on a wheel
hand piercing and chasing of gold and silver
casting and finishing of small links
making.scale: Small workshops in London, Paris and Birmingham; one maker for a whole piece, and a factory for cut steel after about 1760.
making.signs: A closed back, tool marks of the chaser, foil behind each stone and an uneven hand finish on the mount.

pieces.form: Rivière of graduated stones in closed collets
Pierced bow brooch with cut-steel studs
Gold ring with an enamelled band and a plain engraved shoulder
Pearl bracelet with a small painted clasp
Gold locket on a velvet ribbon

positive: foil-backed gemstones in closed silver settings
rivière necklace of graduated paste stones
silk ribbon and velvet at the throat

canonical_works.work: Necklace of the Affair of the Diamond Necklace

evidence.title: A pair of cut steel buckles
Gold and steel watch chain Chatelaine, 19th century (CH 18325499)

emotion.target_response: A calm, formal glitter: the viewer sees small lights in a closed frame, like a room lit by wax candles.

use_cases: costume design for a Regency or Georgian drama
a museum label for a jewel of 1714 to 1837
an image prompt for a candlelit period portrait
avoid_when: the brief wants platinum, geometric lines or open claw settings
the brief wants bold, large, modern stones

modifiers.how: Add jet, hair and engraved lockets, enlarge the pieces and keep the gold and the closed back.
Replace silver and foil with platinum, open the settings and keep the bows and swags.

ornament_level.note: Foil and cut steel give the ornament; plain mourning pieces sit at the low end.
